newsitem.title: GERMANY: N.Europe new crop rapeseed weaker, spot prices up.
newsitem.headline: N.Europe new crop rapeseed weaker, spot prices up.

text.p: Spot rapeseed prices in Northern Europe have gained on a higher Chicago soybean complex but new crop prices are slightly lower, brokers said on Friday.
"Higher nearby prices in Chicago have had their play but that doesn't change crop fundamentals, which point to a good soybean crop this year," one said.
"With soybeans accounting for half the world's oilseeds, that's weighing down rapeseed prices as well."
Buyers free Hamburg were at 487.50 marks a tonne for June, up 7.50 on the week, with sellers at 495.
New crop buyers were at 452.50 marks, down 2.50, while sellers were at 460.
Traders said a large proportion of the new crop had been sold ahead of the harvest to lock in higher prices earlier this year and this was causing prices to drift in the absence of fresh demand.
But price support on the new crop might develop from Polish import interest later in 1997.
Germany's crop weather has been more or less normal but a harsh winter in Poland has damaged the winter rape crop there and this might result in high import demand.
The Warsaw farm ministry said on Monday output may fall to 400,000-450,000 tonnes in 1997 from 500,000 tonnes in 1996 and this would meet only 40 percent of domestic demand.
Rape meal ex Hamburg mills was offered a little firmer in the spot position but the distant months had weakened since last week on seasonally lower demand from the feeds industry.
Animals have been let outside to graze and farmers are cutting grass for silage, traders said.
Corngluten and palmkernel prices were also competitive versus rape meal.
Spot meal was 31.50 marks/100 kg (31-31.25), with June at 29.75 (30.75), first half July at 29.50 (30.50) and August-October at 25.25 (26).
Rape oil sellers were up 2.25 marks on the week for June-July at 94.00 marks and 93.25 for August-October.
